Almost all of the damage was from basements getting flooded. In Chestermere it is mandatory that all houses, no matter where in town they're built, have to have sump pumps. The problem is they don't work when there is no power.

So in a round about way, the lack of power caused the damages, not the water.

How about having some common sense and realizing that rivers rise and not buying into a flood zone. I know Realtors won't tell you that are won't explain that you're buying into a flood zone but come on it takes very little common sense.

Common sense is realizing that Chestermere is not in a flood zone, and that there are no rivers anywhere near it that could or would ever contribute to a flood.

There is a man made canal that leads to a man made lake and then splits off into 2 outlet canals. Which make these next to impossible to flood because you can easily close off the intake and open the 2 outlets. And that's why the canal didn't contribute to the flooding and instead alleviated it.

Even though "City officials are calling the storm a historic event, one that the community only sees about once every 100 years." Chestermere and its residents would have been able to handle it with very few problems if the power would have stayed on even though there was about 8 inches of rain in two hours. Which is remarkable because most other places wouldn't be able to handle something anywhere close to this even with the power on. But of course that's because Chestermere is located on the exact opposite of a flood plain with 2 big man made canals that can quickly and easily drain massive amounts of water away. All that's needed is power to run sump pumps for when 8 inches of water falls in two hours and soaks into the ground.

And like you said - "but come on it takes very little common sense" - to know all of this.
